newsitem.title: UK: UK grain futures down on EU tender, but off lows.
newsitem.headline: UK grain futures down on EU tender, but off lows.

text.p: LIFFE grains ended Friday down, but off lows hit earlier in the day as traders' disappointment with Thursday's limited EU tender award sank in.
May was the most active contract on wheat. It last traded 0.75 stg lower at 98.00, having been as low as 97.25 stg. There were 455 lots of May traded of a total 943 lots of wheat.
"Weekend profit-takers helped it to bounce," one trader said. But the tone remained negative, he said.

Rising sentiment in the new crop, inspired by worries over the lack of rain, had got overdone and this helped it lower, he said. Lower US markets also hit the new crop, he said. "But the die hards are still looking for it to head to the upside rather than down," he said.

Thursday's EU grains management committee awarded 91,200 tonnes of free market soft wheat at a maximum refund of 7.49 ECU per tonne, equivalent to around $167 per tonne fob for French wheat. Traders attacked the award as making EU wheat uncompetitive on the world market. "At this price, you know very well it's not going to be sold," one French trader said.
LIFFE barley also fell. Of 67 lots done, 56 were on November, which last traded 0.50 stg lower at 95.00 stg.
